cold_stub: Plain copper straight into the unit: no shutoff and no flush port, so it cannot be descaled without cutting pipe.
cold_service_port: Boiler drain seized or capped over with paint: soak it, or replace it before the first flush.
heating_chambers: Scale on the elements and chambers. On our water it is a year to this. Descale now and set an annual interval.
front_cover: Read the code and write it down before you touch anything. It is the fastest diagnosis on the truck.
control_board: No heat: breakers, then voltage at the lugs, then the elements and triacs, in that order.
flow_sensor: Flow sensor and inlet screen. Check flow rate and scale before quoting anything.
power_feeds: Read the cable gauge and the breakers in the panel against the plate: an 18 kW unit wants two 40 A double-poles on 8 AWG.
scale_inhibitor: Cartridge past its date or bypassed: it is not treating anything.
surge_protector: Indicator dark or the unit tripped: the protector has done its job once and is finished.
junction_box: Feed comes straight from the panel with nothing on it. One power blink can take out the control board.

inner_tank: Leak from the tank shell. Not repairable: replace the unit.
drain_valve: Drain valve weeping. Cap it or replace the valve.
tp_relief_valve: T&P weeping or seized: pressure or temperature problem, or a tired valve.
hot_water_outlet: Corrosion at the connections: the dielectric is failing.
upper_heating_element: Meter at the terminals: OPEN means no continuity, SHORT to ground trips the breaker.
upper_thermostat: Loose or scorched lugs: heat at a bad connection. Tighten or replace the stat.
high_limit_control: High limit tripped: press the red reset, then find out why it tripped.
lower_thermostat: Water in the compartment: the element gasket or the tank is leaking.
tp_discharge_connection: Discharge must end within 6 in of the floor, full size, gravity only, no threads on the end. PVC here needs to be CPVC or metal.
thermal_expansion_tank: Tank hanging on the pipe with no support: strap it.
drain_pan: Pan fitting with no drain line: the pan can only hold what it holds.
Upper floor or attic: a leak sensor in the pan is the only warning they will get.

ignition_unit: Will not fire: gas, ignition, venting, in that order.
water_manifold: Flow sensor and bypass. Check flow rate, scale, and line sizing before quoting anything.
gas_drip_leg: Read the pipe size at the union against the BTU on the plate. A half inch line runs fine until two fixtures open.
exhaust_vent: Termination clearances: 12 in from a window or door, below a soffit, 3 ft from a dryer vent or air intake.
condensate_neutralizer: Acidic condensate: neutralizer, air gap, and never into a metal pan it will eat.

gas_supply_line: No sediment trap: the drip leg belongs below the shutoff, before the flex. Debris goes into the valve instead.
gas_flex_connector: Old uncoated brass flex: recalled, cracks at the flare. Replace with a coated stainless connector.
gas_shutoff_valve: Shutoff seized or missing: the homeowner cannot isolate this appliance in an emergency.
burner: No flame: pilot out, thermocouple dead, or gas valve failed. Check pilot first.
Soot on the burner or chamber: incomplete combustion. Air, gas pressure, or a blocked flue.
draft_hood: Spillage at the draft hood: flue gases coming back into the room. Stop and fix.
Rust flakes in the hood: condensation has been eating the vent. Inspect the whole run.
vent_pipe: Vent separated at a joint: three screws per joint, pitched up a quarter inch per foot.
Orphaned on an oversized flue: gases cool and spill. Reline or resize the chimney.
top_cover: No working CO detector near a gas appliance. That is a finding every time.
air_intake: Screen packed with lint and dust: the burner is starving for air. Vacuum the screen.
Sealed closet with no combustion air opening: the burner needs air from somewhere.

blower_wheel: A caked crescent on every blade: pull the wheel and chemically clean it. Every bit of that is airflow the house is not getting.
filter_out: Past due. Change it and set up delivery so it is not on them to remember.
Packed solid. Change it, then check the coil and blower for what the restriction already did.
Cut down to fit, air bypassing the frame. Correct the rack so the air actually goes through the media.
filter_base: No filter at all. Install the right size and set the interval.
evap_coil: Matted with dust: airflow loss you can see. Clean the evaporator coil.
Ice is the symptom, not the fault. Diagnose airflow or charge, thaw, and correct.
No coil light. Coil and drain grow biofilm all season. Add a UV coil light.
drain_line: Clogged line, pan filling. Clear and treat the condensate line and check the safety switch.
cabinet: No pan under the unit. Add a pan and a drain line.
No humidity control, so the house rides clammy all summer. Add whole-home dehumidification.
Past repair. Quote the replacement, not another repair.
aux_pan: Pan with nowhere to go. Run the pan drain somewhere they will actually see it.
float_switch: No leak sensor on an attic or upper-floor unit. Add a sensor with automatic shutoff.
dehumidifier: It is here and not doing its job. Service or replace it.
uv_light: UV light fitted but not working. Service or replace it.
disconnect: No surge protection at the equipment. One power blink can take out the board.
surge_protector: Surge device present but not working. Service or replace it.

data_plate: R-22 on the plate: not made anymore, every pound is scarce. The plate alone starts the replacement conversation.
Decode the serial. Past twelve to fifteen years the age goes into the repair math.
condenser_coil: Light dust and grass on the face: a rinse from the inside out at every visit.
Matted with cottonwood or lint: the unit is breathing through a blanket. Head pressure and amps climb every hot afternoon.
Fins combed flat by a weed eater or hail: comb them out, and the lost face is lost capacity.
louver_left: Shrubs or a fence inside 18 inches: it recirculates its own hot air. Clear it.
lineset_insulation_rotted: Suction line sweating bare: lost efficiency every hour it runs, and water where the insulation used to be.
pad: Pad sunk, unit out of level: the compressor runs off level and the lineset is under strain. Lift and re-level.
capacitor: Reads low but still starting: hard starts every cycle and the compressor working overtime. Change it before it takes the compressor.
Failed capacitor, unit will not start. Cheapest part out here.
Older compressor with no hard start assist: every start is a hard pull. A hard start kit or soft start is cheap insurance.
capacitor_bulged: Swollen or domed top: a finding on sight, no meter needed.
disconnect: Heat marks at the disconnect: loose lug or undersized wire. Photograph it, then correct it.
contactor: Contacts pitted and burned: the switch that takes the hit every cycle is wearing out.
Contacts welded closed: the unit never shuts off. Replace the contactor today.
Chattering or buzzing under load: the coil is dying.
whip_entry: Heat browning at the lugs, the wire nuts or the whip: loose connections cook the wire.
compressor: No soft start: every start is a hard inrush that dims the lights and shortens compressor life.
soft_start: Soft start fitted but not doing its job: check the wiring and the fault light.

gas_pipe: Shutoff stiff, union weeping or a joint bubbling on soap. Fix the leak before anything else runs.
No sediment trap below the tee. Grit rides straight into the gas valve. Add the drip leg.
heat_exchanger: Surface rust on the cells, no breach found. Note it and photograph it for next year.
Crack or separation. This one is safety: shut the gas off, red tag, and stop the job.
Rust out or a hole through a cell. Flue gas into the supply air. Shut it down and quote the replacement.
Could not see enough to call it. Say so, and recommend a camera or a combustion test rather than guessing.
burner_assembly: Soot tracking at the burner mouths means the flame is rolling out or the cells are blocked. Find out why before it runs again.
flue: Rust or a loose joint on the vent. Every joint has to be tight and screwed. Rebuild the connector.
A water heater left alone on a chimney sized for both will not draft. Reline or revent the water heater.
inducer: Bearing noise on startup. The inducer is telling you it is going. Quote it before it strands them in January.
co_detector: CO detector present but dead or expired. Replace it today.
No working CO detector in a gas home. Install one on every level.
filter_out: Packed solid, months overdue. Change it, then check the blower and coil for what the restriction already did.
drain_line: Coil drain clogged, pan filling, acid staining the furnace top. Clear and treat the line, check the float.
uv_light: UV lamp fitted but dark or past its year. Replace the bulb.
coil_box: No coil light. The coil and the drain grow biofilm all season. Quote the lamp.

rail_1: This is the whole point of a rail station: the pump is not plumbed in. A claw on its discharge rides the rail down and lands on the base elbow, and the pump's own weight makes the seal. To service it you pull the chain. Nobody goes in the basin.
ball_valve_1: Check valve first, ball valve above it, both up high where a hand reaches them. Shut the ball valve and you can pull the pump or the check with the header still full.
float_lead: Four floats on a tree. STOP keeps the motors under water. LEAD starts a pump. LAG means one pump is losing, so the second joins it. ALARM is above all of them. If the lag float is doing the lead float's job, a float has failed or a pump is weak.
control_board: The 122 swaps the lead pump every cycle so both wear evenly. If one pump does all the work, check that pump's HOA, its breaker, and then put a clamp on it in HAND: 15 amps running is a healthy LSG202M, 53 for an instant as it starts.
contactor_1: Clamp one conductor of a pump in HAND. 15 amps is right. Around 10 with the pump running means it is moving no water: a shut valve, a stuck check, an air lock. Near 8 means it is running dry.
test_button: On the board: CONTROL POWER, LEAD SELECT, TEST and SILENCE, and two glass fuses. F1 is the control fuse, F2 the alarm fuse. Push TEST every visit. A blown F2 means a flooded basin with no warning.

riser: Lids under the grass. Every future service starts with a shovel. Bring the access to grade with a riser.
lid: Cracked lid over a tank of effluent. Replace it today, it is a child safety item.
No bolts in the lid. Anything a child could lift is unsafe. Bolt it or fit a safety pan.
pump: Call the pump in HAND and clamp the amps against the plate. Running is not the same as pumping: watch the level drop.
Drawn down below the pump intake. Something ran that should not have: off float hung, or the panel stuck in HAND.
The check valve is built into the pump head. If the line drains back into the tank after every cycle, that check is gone and the pump is moving the same water twice.
No vault on these. The pump intake screen is the only thing between the tank and the spray heads, so pull the pump and look at it.
float_onoff: One on/off float on a long tether. Lift it with the hook, never a hand in the tank, and prove it starts and stops the pump. Then look at both wires where they leave the riser.
Level up over the float and still rising: the pump is not moving it. No high level float and no panel out here, the aerator alarm at the house is the only warning.
Time a real cycle and measure the drawdown. Gallons per dose, run seconds, cycles a day. The design number belongs to the design.
union: Joint weeping inside the riser. Every dose drops part of itself back in the tank.
uf_cable: No panel at the tank. The pump plugs in at the house on a gray direct burial cable and the float in the tank breaks the hot, so the breaker and the receptacle are at the house. Check them there.
UF-B direct burial cable, gray, no conduit: a cord cap on the house end plugs into the outdoor GFCI receptacle, the cable drops into the trench and runs out to the tank with the rest of the lines.
cord_grip: There is no high level alarm on this tank. The aerator panel at the house is the only alarm the homeowner has, so test that one.

Cord grip through the riser wall below grade: the only hole, and the only place the cable is held. No conduit, no box, no panel out here; the splices hang inside the riser under the lid. The cable comes straight in with a slight fall into the tank, so any water that gets in runs on through, and a bead of sealant goes round it.
spray_head0: Three rotors in a line, 60 ft apart, 30 ft radius each. Every head fires, coverage on target, nothing spraying the fence, the drive, or a window.
spray_head2: Last head set to a full circle: it is spraying over the property line. Set it back to the 180.
splice_hot_to_float_sleeve: Hot to the float: the UF black goes to one lead of the float switch. The float breaks the hot, so with the float down the pump has no power. Clear adhesive lined heat shrink, just bigger than the wire, with a raised section over the barrel: you can see the silver connector through it. Heat it and the adhesive flows and seals it watertight. Click it to slide it back.
splice_float_to_pump_sleeve: Float to pump: the float's other lead to the pump cord's black. Two splices on the hot, one on the neutral, one on the ground, staggered so no two sit side by side.
splice_neutral_sleeve: Neutral straight through: UF white to the pump cord's white.
splice_ground_sleeve: Ground straight through: UF green (or bare) to the pump cord's green.
splice_hot_to_float_crimp: The connection is a 12 AWG butt connector: a silver barrel both conductors go into from the ends and get crimped. It is barely bigger than the wire.
label_float: A label wrapped on each cord, PUMP and FLOAT, reading along the cord, so the next person in the riser knows which is which without tracing them.
label_pump: The pump cord, labelled PUMP: black, white and green, or on some pumps brown hot, blue common and green ground. Its hot comes off the float, its common and ground straight from the UF.
cords: The pump cord and the float wire: up the discharge with a zip tie every foot, over the lip under the lid with a zip tie through its hole (the highest, driest point in the riser), down in a slack loop and straight up into the splices.

riser_pump: Lids under the grass. Three lids and a cleanout on this plant, and every one has to come up on a service. Bring them to grade.
lid_pump: Cracked lid over a tank of effluent. Replace it today, it is a child safety item.
lid_aer: No bolts in the lids. Anything a child could lift is unsafe. Bolt every one or fit safety pans.
blower: Hand on the blower. Running, warm, moving air. It runs 24 hours a day: an ATU with the blower off has been a septic tank since the day it stopped.
Running but weak. Diaphragms wear, the filter chokes. Pull the filter cover first, then check the output at the air line.
tank_section: Open the aeration lid. Healthy is a steady roll and liquor light to dark brown. Gray or black with a sour smell means no treatment has happened in a while.
blower_filter_cover: Foam element under the cover on top of the blower. Clean it every 3 months. Packed solid, it starves the blower and the tank.
aeration_pipe: Diffuser bar on the floor under the air drop. Weak or no bubbling with the blower running means it is clogged: pull it up the aeration hatch and clean the orifices.
surge_device: Plug in surge protector at the post receptacle. Lightning takes out more air pumps and spray pumps than anything else out here.
chlorinator: Tablet tube through the slab where the clarifier water crosses into the pump room. Pull the cap: tablets stacked, water touching the bottom one, feeding.
Tube empty. Nothing has been disinfected since the last tablet went. Load septic tablets (calcium hypochlorite) and note it.
chlor_pool_tablets: Pool tablets in the tube. Trichlor is the wrong chemistry and gasses off in a closed tank. Pull them, ventilate, load septic tablets.
pump: Call the pump in HAND and clamp the amps. Running is not the same as pumping: watch the level in the pump room drop.
No vault on these. The pump intake screen is the only thing between the pump room and the heads, so pull the pump on the union and look at it.
float_onoff: One on/off float on a tether. Lift it with the hook and prove it starts and stops the pump. Then look at both wires where they leave the riser.
spray_head0: Three rotors in a line, 60 ft apart, 30 ft radius each. Every head fires and pops down, coverage on target, nothing spraying the fence, the drive, or a window.
Standing water at the base: the swing pipe or the head seal is leaking, or the pattern is too heavy for the ground.
spray_head2: Last head set to a full circle: it is spraying over the property line. Set it back to the 180.
spray_head1: Head cut off or missing. The other two carry the whole dose, so they overload their patterns and the yard puddles.
union: Joint weeping inside the riser. Every dose drops part of itself back in the tank.
uf_cable: UF-B direct burial cable, gray, no conduit: a cord cap on the house end plugs into the outdoor GFCI receptacle, the cable drops into the trench and runs out to the tank with the rest of the lines.
cord_grip: Cord grip through the riser wall below grade, on the house side: the only hole, and the only place the cable is held. No conduit, no box, no panel out here; the splices hang inside the riser under the lid. The cable comes straight in with a slight fall into the tank, so any water that gets in runs on through, and a bead of sealant goes round it.
splice_hot_to_float_sleeve: Hot to the float: the UF black goes to one lead of the float switch. The float breaks the hot, so with the float down the pump has no power. Clear adhesive lined heat shrink, just bigger than the wire, with a raised section over the barrel: you can see the silver connector through it. Heat it and the adhesive flows and seals it watertight. Click it to slide it back.
splice_float_to_pump_sleeve: Float to pump: the float's other lead to the pump cord's black. Two splices on the hot, one on the neutral, one on the ground, staggered so no two sit side by side.
splice_neutral_sleeve: Neutral straight through: UF white to the pump cord's white.
splice_ground_sleeve: Ground straight through: UF green (or bare) to the pump cord's green.
splice_hot_to_float_crimp: The connection is a 12 AWG butt connector: a silver barrel both conductors go into from the ends and get crimped. It is barely bigger than the wire.
label_float: A label wrapped on each cord, PUMP and FLOAT, reading along the cord, so the next person in the riser knows which is which without tracing them.
label_pump: The pump cord, labelled PUMP: black, white and green, or on some pumps brown hot, blue common and green ground. Its hot comes off the float, its common and ground straight from the UF.
cords: The pump cord and the float wire: up the discharge with a zip tie every foot, over the lip under the lid with a zip tie through its hole (the highest, driest point in the riser), down in a slack loop and straight up into the splices.

handle_loose: Wallows in the hole. Replace the handle before the day it stops lifting the flapper.
chain_loose: Too much slack: the flapper does not lift clean and the flush takes two tries. Set it to a half inch of slack, or replace the flapper and set the chain.
chain_broken: Chain or lift wire broken. The handle does nothing until this is replaced.
flapper_bad: Warped and scaled, never seals. The tank refills every few minutes: this is the running toilet.
seat_scaled: Seat scaled over so the flapper cannot land flat. Replace the flush valve.
tank_water_high: Water over the overflow tube: it drains into the bowl around the clock. Set the level a half inch below the top of the overflow, replace the fill valve if it will not hold.
bowl_water_dyed: Color in the bowl ten minutes after dyeing the tank: the flush valve is leaking by, day and night.
fill_valve: Slow fill. Replace the fill valve.
Hisses and never fully stops. Replace the fill valve.
ballcock: Old ballcock, no anti-siphon. Replace it with a current anti-siphon fill valve.
angle_stop: Stop will not turn by hand. It is the one valve that has to work the day the line lets go. Replace it.
stop_crust: Green crust and a damp ring: it has been weeping for a while. Replace the stop and line.
supply_line_old: Old braided line, corroded or bulging. These let go with nobody home. Replace it.
angle_stop_multiturn: Multi-turn stop that has never been exercised. Swap it for a quarter-turn.
bolts_seep: Seeping at the tank bolts. It stains the floor slowly for years. New bolts and washers.
base_gap: Rocks front to back: the wax seal is compromised. Pull, reset with a new seal, shim it solid.
base_stain: Water staining at the base. The seal has been leaking under the bowl.
soft_floor: Soft or spongy around the flange. The subfloor is what gets expensive; it needs to come up.
flange_broken: Flange broken or below the finished floor. Repair ring or new flange before it goes back down.
bidet_seat: Their bidet seat is not working right. Check the outlet and the tee first.
seat: It is in the Happy Homes Guide. Mention it while you are already at the toilet; check for an outlet within reach.

trash_tank.name: Trash Tank (in front of the plant)

tank: A trash tank is a small septic tank in front of the aerobic plant. It holds back what will not break down (grease, wipes, the heavy solids) so the plant only has to treat the liquid.
riser: Lid under the grass. Every future pump out starts with a shovel. Bring the access to grade with a riser.
lid: Cracked lid over a full tank. Replace it today, it is a child safety item.
inlet: Look at the inlet tee with the lid off: the drop must be there and open. A missing inlet tee lets the incoming flow stir the scum and push it toward the outlet.
outlet: The outlet tee sits 3 in under the inlet and dips into the clear middle. If it is missing or broken, scum and solids go straight into the plant and foul its aeration and its pump.
water: Measure the scum and the sludge. When they fill a third of the tank it is time to pump it, or the solids carry over into the plant. The trash tank gets pumped more often than the plant.
Normal level is the bottom of the outlet pipe. Liquid up in the riser means the outlet or the line to the plant is blocked. Low means the tank is leaking.

monitor_body: An air quality monitor tells the homeowner what the air in the house is doing: CO2, chemicals (VOC), fine dust, humidity and temperature. It is how they see the filter, the fresh air and the purifier working.
wall_bracket: Mount it on an inside wall in the main living space, about thermostat height, out of sun, away from supply registers, kitchens and bath doors. Keep 2 in clear on both sides for the vents.
readings_a: Read the numbers with the homeowner: CO2 under 1000 ppm, humidity 40 to 60 percent, PM2.5 under 12. High CO2 means not enough fresh air. High PM2.5 means the filter is not catching it.
display_poor: Red ring: poor air. Check the filter, the fresh air duct and the return, and talk about ventilation, a media filter or a purifier.
pm_sensor: Inside: a laser dust sensor with its own small fan pulls air in the left slots, past the CO2, VOC and humidity sensors, and out the right grille. Dust or tape over the slots gives wrong readings.
adapter: Power: the 5 V adapter in the outlet under it, the cable in the cord channel. A blank screen is almost always the adapter pulled out or the outlet dead. Check the outlet before you blame the monitor.
bracket_screws: Slide the monitor up to lift it off its wall mount. Two screws in anchors hold the mount.

centre_tube: Lid off: a strong bubble plume over the unit, liquid rising through the centre. Weak or none, go to the pump.
blend_bag: Pull the bag: a grey-brown coating 1/16 in or more is healthy. Black means pull the unit and hose it out.
column: Probe the sludge and the scum: over 12 in of either, pump the tank.
air_pump: Pump running and humming; shut it off and the alarm should come on. Turn it back on before you leave.
receptacle_gfci: No air: test and reset the GFCI first.
clear_tube: Clear tube and clamps tight, no kink; listen for leaks at the joints.
control_box: Alarm lit and the power light dark: the pump has stopped. Likeliest cause is a torn diaphragm.
air_union: Open the union to lift the unit out on its rope for cleaning.
